beur-hagra.1#א: 24, etc. Jerusalem Talmud, chapter 7 of Shevi'is, halacha 24: that whose prohibition is by Torah law, it is forbidden to engage in commerce with it; and that whose prohibition is by rabbinic law, it is permitted to engage in commerce with it. And a donkey is raised for its labor, and a camel is raised for its labor. R' Hoshaya carried and gave in this morais; R' Huna carried and gave in this chilteis— meaning, they would engage in buying and selling with chilteis and morais, which are by rabbinic law. And likewise, in the Tosefta, chapter 5: one should not bring dogs, kofrin, squirrels’ weasels, cats, and a hedgehog to sell them to a non-Jew, and to ride upon them; but morais, and the cheeses of Beit Huniki, and their bread and their oil, it is permitted to sell them and to lie upon them.
beur-hagra.1#ב: Even though, etc. The above Tosefta, and the Mishnah there: “and not with neveilos, etc.” and all of them are permitted for benefit, as written in the chapter Kol Sha'ah.
beur-hagra.1#ג: Or, etc. Terumat HaDeshen is in doubt regarding this.
beur-hagra.1#ד: And even to purchase it, etc. At the end of the first chapter of Avodah Zarah, daf 62a: “shall we say that we give, etc.” and the Torah says, etc.; and Tosafos there, daf 63a, s.v. “and it is not,” and it is difficult— who, etc.; therefore it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ה: And likewise, one who, etc. As written: “to the convert, etc., or sell to a non-Jew.”
beur-hagra.1#ו: Provided, etc. Mishnah there: R' Yehudah says, etc., and the Sages forbid; and the Rambam explained there that R' Yehudah permits when he intends to trap.
beur-hagra.1#ז: And he must sell it, etc. From what is written in Bava Kamma, chapter 1, and likewise: “to the convert, etc.” specifically in such a case.
beur-hagra.1#ח: And likewise it is permitted, etc. For this reason we collect from them on their festival day; and see Tosafos in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah, daf 2a, s.v. “and to collect,” etc.
beur-hagra.1#ט: And it is forbidden, etc. Chapter Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 94).
